name: step2-feature-availability
notes: STEP 2 of the three-step data selection: which feature families exist on the step-1 dates. Inputs are a ticker (foreach.keys), the same prepared panel as step 1, and step 1's selected.jsonl onboarded through source-step1-selection.json. The cohort is step 1's dates at step 1's selected DTE: that DTE is read from step 1's output and never typed, and the cohort refuses (agreed_dte) when its date count differs from step 1's recorded listed_dates, i.e. when the source or ticker changed between the two steps. implied_cdf is ONE of 13 families: a missing CDF, an ineligible proxy or an absent field is a gap on that date, never a cohort filter. Outputs in pipeline_runs/step2-feature-availability: dates.jsonl lists each cohort date with its available_<family> yes/no flags (the per-date gaps); combinations.jsonl has one row per subset of the 13 families, 8,192 per ticker, where with_<f>=1 means family f is in the combination and dates is the number of distinct cohort dates on which EVERY included family is yes (the all-zero row is the cohort total); carry.json holds summary_<family>__<t> (per-family counts) and cohort_summary__<t>. A date with two different availability patterns refuses rather than count twice. Memory: the fan-out is at most (distinct patterns + 1) x 2^13 rows. Finite values give no historical known-at certification: observation clocks stay in family_contracts. For AMZN only the CDF family is materialized; the others are gaps, not proof the sources are absent.

source.notes: THE DATA SOURCE: the onboarded prepared option panel, named by root/source/stream and resolved from the working directory. Another panel changes these values and nothing else. Both child runbooks onboard their own panel under these same names (index_options reuses its cdf-horizon-source acquisition; stock_options imports the AMZN panel there), so this file runs unchanged from either child. key_fields is the panel's row identity: rows that differ only elsewhere (AMZN rows differing only by price_basis) collide and refuse loudly instead of one being chosen silently. ts_out is quote_date_ms, not the default asof_ms, because the AMZN panel already carries asof_ms and ObservationRows refuses to overwrite a field.

step1_selection.notes: The onboarded copy of step 1's selected.jsonl (source-step1-selection.json): one winner row per ticker. The selected DTE and its date count are read from here, so this step can never run at a typed horizon.

implied_cdf.clock: after-close reconstruction; no intraday availability claim

return_history.lookback: 22 prior exchange-session returns including entry close

ohlc_shape.lookback: up to 22 OHLC sessions plus prior close
ohlc_shape.clock: requires full-cohort materialization from local OHLC source

volatility_context.lookback: last observation within configured maximum age (7 calendar days)
volatility_context.clock: date-level backward join; release timestamp not certified

expanded_volatility_context.lookback: last observation within 7 calendar days; duplicate VXN omitted
expanded_volatility_context.clock: requires full-cohort materialization and release-clock audit

surface_changes.lookback: 1/5/22 prior observations within expiry, not necessarily exchange sessions
surface_changes.clock: same-series backward changes; term slope ordering used realized DTE, needs prospective scheduled-DTE rebuild

variance_gap.lookback: same-expiry IV, scheduled sessions, prior 22-session variance
variance_gap.clock: requires full-cohort materialization from existing fields

liquidity.clock: after-close snapshot proxies, not executable quotes or signed dealer positions

positioning_changes.lookback: same snapshot plus prior same-contract open interest
positioning_changes.clock: requires full-cohort materialization and OI publication-clock audit

macro_context.lookback: daily sources lagged one declared exchange session; weekly seven days; age guards
macro_context.clock: historical release/vintage not certified; finite values are not proof of entry-known availability

chain_nodes.lookback: same entry chain within configured moneyness gap
chain_nodes.clock: after-close reconstruction; all nine masks required for full-family completeness

family_contracts.notes: Hash-bound field groups, lookback requirements and clock limits. Split broad families into separately testable materialization/quality subgroups. implied_cdf also requires rn_proxy_eligible == 1: the step-2 cohort now includes dates whose proxy was rejected upstream, and a rejected proxy is an unavailable CDF.

implied_cdf_21.reason: Exact probability grid not preregistered; recompute from original chains, never interpolate nine inputs to claim 21 observations

implied_cdf_41.reason: Exact probability grid not preregistered; recompute from original chains

macro_events.reason: No local historical event calendar carrying known-at timestamps

params.provenance_waiver: each row carries its own symbol; the key check proves no ticker appears twice

params.source: One row per cohort date and ticker with its 13 available_<family> yes/no flags: the per-date family gaps on step 1's selected dates

date_evidence.notes: Refuses to overwrite and needs its parent directory; move pipeline_runs/step2-feature-availability aside to repeat.

params.provenance_waiver: each row carries its own symbol; the key check proves no ticker appears twice

params.source: Distinct cohort dates for every one of the 2^13 family combinations, 8,192 rows per ticker; with_<f>=1 means family f is in the combination

combination_evidence.notes: Refuses to overwrite and needs its parent directory; move pipeline_runs/step2-feature-availability aside to repeat.

foreach.notes: The only ticker setting, and it must match step 1's: a ticker absent from step 1's selection refuses. AMZN is ["AMZN"], run from children/stock_options. No per-ticker copies of this file exist or are needed.

selection.notes: This ticker's winner row from step 1.

selected_dte.notes: The DTE step 2 runs at, read from step 1. An empty table (ticker absent from step 1) leaves a dangling reference below and the run refuses.

selected_dates.notes: Step 1's recorded date count at that DTE, used only to pin this run's cohort to it.

cohort.notes: Step 1's cohort predicate (symbol, settled) at step 1's DTE. No feature or CDF clause may ever be added here: availability is measured on this cohort, not used to choose it.

cohort_summary.notes: The cohort's own date count and bounds, retained in carry.json.

agreement.notes: Keeps the summary only when this run's cohort date count equals step 1's listed_dates.

agreed_dte.notes: Empty when the counts disagree, which makes the reference below dangle.

checked_cohort.notes: A tautology when step 1 and step 2 agree; on disagreement the dangling agreed_dte reference refuses the run, so step 2 can never describe other dates than step 1.

check_implied_cdf.notes: yes when every implied_cdf field is finite and its quality checks hold; else no. The flag tests materialized finite completeness only, never historical known-at certification.

summary_implied_cdf.notes: Per-family yes/no date counts; an absent group has zero dates.

date_patterns.notes: One row per cohort date with its 13 family flags: the per-date gaps, written to dates.jsonl. Expiries on one date with the same pattern collapse into one row.

one_pattern_per_date.notes: Refuses when a date has two different patterns: a date must count once.

patterns.notes: The distinct availability patterns and how many dates share each.

universe_flags.notes: One extra all-yes row, given zero weight below, so every one of the 2^13 subsets appears in combinations.jsonl even when no date satisfies it.

expand_implied_cdf.notes: Each pattern row fans out to the combinations it can join: a family that is yes may be in or out of a combination, one that is no can only be out. Chained over the 13 families this enumerates every subset a pattern satisfies.

combinations.notes: Distinct dates per combination: the sum over patterns of the dates sharing a pattern, exact because each date has exactly one pattern. 8,192 rows per ticker.
